strengths: A complete workstation retains a coherent bench, populated tool board and rolling storage silhouette in both unrelated interiors.
The physical vise, bench dogs, drawer handles, castors, loose surface items and hanging-tool silhouettes provide readable inhabited-world detail without texture or renderer lock-in.
Warm historic and cool contemporary treatments preserve wood, steel, painted metal and brass separation through bounded reuse of the verified warm-interior lighting rig.
All three assets remain fully visible through three materially different camera landmarks while the declared operator corridor stays clear.
limitations: The hand tools and peg pattern are simplified medium-distance silhouettes and are not accepted for close-up or hero insert photography.
The verification hosts intentionally prove transfer and lighting response; they are not publishable finished room environments.
Drawers, wheels, vise and loose tools are static geometry in this release; no animated interaction or physics behavior is claimed.
notes: V1 was rejected because distant cameras made the physical details too small to judge. V2 established the accepted closer composition but exposed a camera outside the contemporary host, producing a 79% black semantic frame. V3 clamps all cameras inside host walls, retains the stricter eight-percent entity-height gate, and is accepted only at medium/background shot distance.
